title: NEB Class 11 Physics — Ideal Gas — 2024
subject: physics
source: NEB Grade 11 Model Questions / NEB Past Papers 2020-2024

questions.question: State the kinetic theory of gases. Also state its assumptions.
questions.solution:
**Kinetic theory:** gas pressure arises from countless molecular collisions with the container walls; pressure is proportional to the average kinetic energy of the molecules.

**Assumptions:** (1) huge number of molecules in random motion; (2) molecules are point masses of negligible volume; (3) no intermolecular forces except during collisions; (4) collisions are perfectly elastic; (5) collision time is negligible; (6) molecules move uniformly between collisions.
questions.knowledgeNote: Kinetic theory gives P = (1/3)ρ⟨v²⟩ — pressure from density times mean-square speed.

questions.question: What is the law of equipartition of energy? How many degrees of freedom does a monoatomic gas molecule have?
questions.solution:
**Equipartition:** at thermal equilibrium, energy is shared equally among all degrees of freedom, each getting (1/2)kT per molecule.

A monoatomic molecule has **3 translational** degrees of freedom (x, y, z), so its molar heat at constant volume is Cv = (3/2)R.
questions.knowledgeNote: Diatomic adds 2 rotational → 5 degrees; vibrational modes unfreeze only at high temperatures.

questions.question: Calculate the rms speed of oxygen molecules at 27°C. (Molar mass of O₂ = 32 g/mol, R = 8.31 J/mol·K)
questions.knowledgeNote: v_rms = √(3RT/M): lighter gases and higher temperatures mean faster molecules — Graham's law of diffusion follows directly.

questions.question: State Boyle's law, Charles's law, and the pressure law. Combine them to obtain the ideal gas equation.
questions.solution:
**Boyle (T const):** V ∝ 1/P. **Charles (P const):** V ∝ T. **Pressure law (V const):** P ∝ T.

Together V ∝ T/P, i.e. PV/T = constant. For n moles the constant is nR:

**PV = nRT** — the ideal gas equation.
questions.knowledgeNote: T must be in kelvin — the laws fail on the Celsius scale because the proportionality needs a true zero.

questions.question: Two moles of an ideal gas at 300 K occupy 0.05 m³. Calculate its pressure. (R = 8.31 J/mol·K)
questions.knowledgeNote: One mole at STP (0°C, 1 atm) occupies 22.4 L — a instant check for gas-arithmetic answers.

questions.question: Calculate the average kinetic energy per molecule of a gas at 300 K. (k = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K)
questions.knowledgeNote: Temperature IS average molecular KE — this single formula is the bridge between the microscopic and macroscopic pictures.
